outOfScopeFindingNOTFixed.status: 2 of 9 tests now fail (sphere-crosshatch, cone-crosshatch 'mean rendered bearing is stable across Density 50->150'); NOT in this unit's ALLOWED file list, NOT edited
outOfScopeFindingNOTFixed.measured: sphere gap 3.70deg (was 0.57deg), cone gap 3.82deg (was 0.06deg); tolerance is 3deg
outOfScopeFindingNOTFixed.rootCause: mathematically explained, not a placement bug: this guard's 'stability' metric is the COMBINED length-weighted bearing of both crosshatch families. Before W-36 family A held ~91% of the ink share, so the combined bearing was dominated by (and effectively measured only) family A's own direction field. W-36 intentionally moves the split toward 50/50 (measured shareA 0.47-0.52 across Density 50/150 on sphere/cone) - averaging two bearings that are themselves nearly orthogonal (measured per-family: sphere bearingA 63.0->62.1deg, bearingB 168.71->168.72deg between Density 50 and 150; cone bearingA 84.4->83.1deg, bearingB 144.18->144.18deg - EACH family's own direction field is stable to <1.5deg, exactly the property this guard file's docstring says it exists to verify). A near-50/50 vector average of two near-orthogonal bearings is maximally sensitive to a small (2-3%) shift in the ink-share ratio between the two families, which is what produces the combined-metric swing. Cylinder and torus crosshatch (not near a 50/50-orthogonal cancellation point at this fillAngle) still pass.
outOfScopeFindingNOTFixed.recommendation: orchestrator decision needed: either accept as an inherent, understood consequence of shipping crosshatch parity (and have a follow-up unit redesign that guard to check each family's bearing separately, which is what it actually intends to guard), or something else. Not touched here — outside this unit's ALLOWED file list and not named in the plan's guard list.
